description: Henley Passport Index 2026: Iran ranked 90th, visa-free or visa-on-arrival to 40 destinations. Other indices rank it as low as 190th depending on whether eVisa and visa-on-arrival are counted.
notes: Indices disagree because they count different things. Henley is the usual citation; state the index when quoting a rank.

description: Iranian passport holders cannot enter the UAE, Libya, Syria or the United States on the passport alone - the UAE exclusion matters most in practice because Dubai is a common transit and visa-interview hub.
Because nothing is visa-free, every trip - including a trip taken only to attend another country's visa interview - needs its own application, fee, biometrics appointment and travel.
money_note: Compounding: each leg is a separate fee.
time_note: Per application, in parallel where allowed.

description: Conference attendance, client meetings, on-site interviews and family events are all gated. The professional cost is invisible on paper: the invitations stop coming once a person is known to be hard to move.
notes: Frequently described in diaspora accounts; not quantified here.

aspect: SCENARIO - the conference Omid cannot attend
description: Omid's paper is accepted at a conference in Lisbon in May. The Schengen application needs an appointment in Yerevan, three months' bank statements he cannot produce, and eight weeks he does not have. He withdraws the paper and his supervisor presents it. His name stays on it; his face is not in the room.
energy_note: Published, and absent from your own work.
